scope: The original 24 LMX source files and the existing Analogies.hs only. No LMX or Haskell implementation was added or rewritten for this index.
coverage_unit: An existing source example, including its current specified cases. complete_pair denotes the explicitly bounded full common fixture, not equivalence of entire language/runtime architectures.

status_definitions.complete_pair: An existing extracted Haskell implementation covers the full declared common fixture. Numeric packing/Bool normalization is explicit; imports and all called user definitions are included.
status_definitions.related_analogy: Existing Haskell code illustrates the behavior but lacks a material current case/mechanism, or its inseparable instrumentation prevents a fair source-count boundary. No numerical comparison ratio is authorized.
status_definitions.lmx_only: No existing Haskell implementation for this source example. A similar different guide example is not silently substituted.

extraction_policy: Function/type declarations and case expressions are exact lines from Analogies.hs; complete listings contain no new helper definitions. Import selectors may be narrowed to the required existing symbols; each normalized import records its original source line. main/assertEq and unrelated examples are not duplicated into each pair. M01 compares service code only on both sides. H04 includes its four-probe expression because the LMX listing also contains those calls. H09 has no ratio because its Haskell algorithm and extra counter instrumentation are inseparable without rewriting the uploaded function.
measurement_policy: Counts include shown comments and all non-whitespace characters; physical/nonempty lines and UTF-8 bytes are also reported. Full module is measured once, separately from per-pair listings. Ratios are permitted only for complete_pair; related_analogy/lmx_only must remain blank or N/A.

entries.title: Replace and invoke a first-class callable
entries.foreign_code:
import Data.IORef (newIORef, readIORef)
import qualified Data.IORef as Ref

applicationExample :: IO Int
applicationExample = do
  chosen <- newIORef ((*2) :: Int -> Int)
  firstOperation <- readIORef chosen
  let first = firstOperation 7
  Ref.writeIORef chosen (+1)
  secondOperation <- readIORef chosen
  let second = secondOperation 7
  pure (first * 100 + second)
entries.contract_notes: Complete for the current successful fixture: store twice, read and invoke it with 7, replace the same callable cell by plusOne, read and invoke it with 7; packed result 1408. IORef is a real base facility. The Haskell IO wrapper expresses the two writes/reads explicitly; no claim about the full LMX callable ABI is made.

entries.title: Independent bound prefixes and residual callable admission

makeAdder :: Int -> Int -> Int
makeAdder n = (+) n

closureExample :: (Int, Int, Int)
closureExample =
  let add5 = makeAdder 5
      add100 = makeAdder 100
  in (add5 1, add100 1, add5 1)
entries.contract_notes: Complete captured-prefix fixture: add5 and add100 are independent, their results are 6,101,6, and the original addition remains unchanged. Haskell values are immutable and native partial application exposes only the remaining argument. The LMX-specific explicit saved actual is rejected by its residual signature; Haskell has no such named formal and rejects that spelling statically. This admission-language difference is recorded separately and does not subtract the matching successful fixture.

entries.title: Whole ASCII ticket-code predicate
entries.foreign_code:
import Data.Ix (inRange)

accepts :: String -> Bool
accepts [a,b,'-',c,d] =
  all (inRange ('A','Z')) [a,b]
    && all (inRange ('0','9')) [c,d]
accepts _ = False
entries.contract_notes: Complete whole-string predicate for exactly two ASCII uppercase letters, hyphen, two ASCII digits. The five-element list pattern enforces length; inRange checks ASCII endpoints. All eleven current fixtures agree, including NUL, non-ASCII letter and non-ASCII digit rejection. Haskell String and LMX char[] use their ordinary character-sequence representations; no locale-dependent character class is introduced.

entries.title: Serial state updates at one Message owner
entries.foreign_code:
import Control.Concurrent (MVar, putMVar)
import Control.Concurrent.Chan (Chan, readChan)

data CounterRequest = AddBy Int (MVar Int) | ReadValue (MVar Int) | Stop (MVar ())

counterLoop :: Chan CounterRequest -> Int -> IO ()
counterLoop inbox value = do
  request <- readChan inbox
  case request of
    AddBy delta reply -> do
      let next = value + delta
      next `seq` putMVar reply next
      counterLoop inbox next
    ReadValue reply -> do
      putMVar reply value
      counterLoop inbox value
    Stop ack -> putMVar ack ()
entries.contract_notes: Complete local-owner fixture: one owner, two sender threads submit additions 4 and 9, each accepted request has one serialized update, final read occurs after both responses and returns 13 for either arrival order. The counted Haskell service uses actual Chan/MVar facilities and includes its owner loop and existing Stop acknowledgement branch. counterExample launches/sends/observes/stops it only as an external verification harness and is excluded from this service-to-service count, just as the LMX sender/owner launcher is outside Counter. The LMX fixture relies on the existing Message owner launcher. Neither side of this local comparison is credited with a complete HTTP or distributed-delivery stack; the separate HTTP profile remains outside this ratio.
